incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired (PD: PD-83219) — inference-eu-embeddings 5xx spike (count=324, last=30s). Auto-escalate to oncall: @Asha

Asha: acked via pagerbot, I'm taking initial ownership. digging into kvcache and ingress metrics.

pagerbot: Acknowledged: Asha (on-call). Escalation policy: inference-platform -> eng-oncall -> eng-sre.

Tom: pinging here — any customer-facing signals? I can start collecting request traces if needed.

Asha: initial look: spike concentrated in eu-west-1 ingestion cluster, 503s mainly for batch-embed API. latency graphs showing queue depth jump. attaching quick dump below.

Maya: customers reporting timeouts in EU region, saw two support tickets mentioning batch jobs failing. ETA for mitigation?

Asha: triage steps: 1) confirm upstream SLOs failing 2) check autoscaler 3) if autoscale not catching, do manual scale/bounce 4) consider routing to fallback region.

Eli: if autoscaler is stuck we might have a race where multiple workers spin up but never register due to mistaken healthcheck. saw similar last month.

Tom: running query against metrics: `sum(rate(kv_cache_errors_total[1m])) by (pod)` — getting elevated error for pod inference-eu-7.

Asha: good catch. I'm ssh-ing to inference-eu-7 now, tailing logs. grabbing stack traces.

incident-bot: PagerDuty note: PD-83219 escalated to ENG-SRE. Recorder started.

Asha: logs show OOM eviction then kube restarted the container repeatedly. healthcheck failing on readiness probe due to KV cache init error: `failed to mmap cache file: file too large`

Maya: customer impact: ~15% of embed requests in eu-west-1 are returning 503s. Most customers degrade to retries; we should proactively message support for affected accounts.

Tom: proposal: cordon the node, force pods to reschedule to nodes with higher disk, and bump autoscaler buffer. Also apply a temporary cache-size override per-pod env var to avoid mmap growth.

Eli: +1 to cache-size override. I can push a canary rollout with `CACHE_MAX_BYTES=200000000` to 2 pods in eu-west-1.

Asha: doing the canary now — patching deployment: `kubectl set env deploy/inference-eu CACHE_MAX_BYTES=200000000 --record` and scaling to 4 replicas to test.

Tom: while canary rolls, I'll open a routing rule to send new embed requests from a subset of customers to eu-central as fallback (low-risk). command: `redwood route-mod --from eu-west-1 --to eu-central --filter=acct in (acct1,acct2)`

Maya: notifying support: `support@redwood` please start templated outbound for accounts showing increased 503. add note: mitigation in progress, expect partial routing/fallback.

Asha: canary looks healthy after 90s, no mmap errors in logs, latency normal. scaling remaining replicas with same env var.

pagerbot: Asha acknowledged change. Alert noise suppressed for 10m.

Tom: routing change applied for two high-impact customers. we should monitor error budget and rollback if anything odd.

Eli: autoscaler backlog cleared after pods stabilized. queue depth trending back down.

Maya: support confirmed reduced ticket volume after routing + canary. still some retries but acceptable.

Asha: summary update for PD ticket: root cause potential: KV cache mmap growth on specific node type causing OOM + readiness failures => pod restart loop => autoscaler lag. Mitigation: temporary per-pod cache limit + node cordon/reschedule + targeted routing fallback.

Tom: handoff plan: Asha will continue monitoring for 30m, then hand to Tom for follow-up (kernel/fs review + infra RAID check).

Asha: handing to Tom at 1832110200. leaving note: watch pv usage and mmap error rate.

Tom: acknowledged handoff. I'll take it from here and open a post-incident ticket to track root cause and long-term fix (increase disk, shard cache file, add readiness guard).

incident-bot: PD-83219 status updated: acknowledged -> mitigated. Incident timeline recorded.

Maya: thanks everyone — I'll draft a short blameless note for support and send to affected customers.

Eli: quick ping 10m: no regressions observed.

Asha: thanks all, closing my active claim. if anything flares I'll re-open. :thumbsup:
